utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Can we have the appearances on behalf of the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. For the Prosecution, Tecla Henry-Benjamin, and case manager, Andres Vatter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for the Defence, please, who are almost all present. Could they be kind enough to introduce themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to my colleagues from the Prosecution. For Defence of General Hadzihasanovic, Stephane Bourgon, assisted by Alexis Demirdjian, legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And for the other Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Today representing Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon and Fahrudin Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Upon the resumption of this hearing, which will be the last of this part of the case, which started in July and continued in October, the Chamber bids good morning to all those present, the representatives of the Prosecution, and particularly Madam Benjamin, the representatives of the Defence, the accused, and all the staff of this courtroom, Mr. Registrar, the legal assistant, the usher, Madam Court Reporter, as well as all the interpreters in the booths, and of course I do not wish to leave out the security officers. We have several points to address during this hearing, and I shall address each of them. But as for the first point, I should like to deal with it in private session. Could we, therefore, Mr. Registrar, go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you know, the Chamber on the 16th of July, 2004 issued a decision concerning the admissibility of certain contested documents and those marked for identification. This written decision is -- has two attachments, Annex A and Annex B. With a view to the numbering of the documents admitted, there was close coordination of views between the registrar, the legal officer of the Chamber, and the Prosecution, and there appears to be a little problem outstanding concerning some documents; that is, the diaries of the 7th Brigade, some of the paragraphs having been translated, but not the totality of that diary. And that is why the Prosecution needs to tell us that -- whether they are requesting the admission only the parts that have been translated. By way of example, a document from the diary of the 7th Brigade, page 15 has been translated. It is a diary published in February 1993. Whereas, we have the totality of that diary. And there are several documents which have only partially been translated. So I'd like to ask Madam Benjamin to tell us whether she is withdrawing the nontranslated paragraphs. Madam Benjamin.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Good morning again to Mr. President and Your Honours. Mr. President, it is the Prosecution's decision that the diaries, the journals, will be withdrawn, leaving only the articles with the relevant P numbers, so we are making the application to have those withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Madam Benjamin. We take note of what you are telling us. Today, with regard to these documents, by an oral decision the Chamber says the following: The Chamber rendered its written decision regarding the admissibility of documents on the 16th of July, 2004. The Chamber subsequently noted that paragraph 79 of its written decision does not correspond to Annex A of that decision, because the document bearing the number 582 was withdrawn by the Prosecution. Due to this fact, the paragraph 79 will be corrected as follows, and I'm going to read the sentence appearing in paragraph 79: "The contested document 582 was withdrawn by the Prosecution." Furthermore, as indicated in paragraph 64 of this decision, a single number will be given for contested documents as follows: There are six categories of contested documents in paragraph 64, documents 10, 11, 12, 13, 163, 174, and 445. These documents will be re-grouped under a single number, and the registrar will indicate that number in a moment. The same applies for document 20, 27, 28, 229, 288, and 297, which will also be given a single number, which we will have in a moment. And the third group are document 231, 240, 339, and 345, which will also have a single number. The fourth category, consisting of documents 173, 243, 346, and 557, which will be given a single number; the fifth category consisting of three documents, 141, 350, 452, will have one number; and finally, the last category, consisting of only two documents, 555, and 556, and the two will also be given a single number. Furthermore, the registrar, which did a great deal of work, noted that minor errors are contained in Annex A with respect to the ERN numbers or the dates of the exhibits. There are some errors with respect to the numbers mentioned in the column that you have in front of you, Annex A, column 4, B/C/S ERN numbers. So there are a few numbers there indicated in Annex A which are erroneous, and also some documents containing erroneous dates. So a written decision of a corrigendum will be filed at the beginning of next week containing references to the corrected paragraph 79, as I have just indicated, and also a correction of Annex A. So we will have a corrected Annex A, which will correct the few minor errors that crept in. Finally, at the beginning of the week there will also be a public version of the decision, and this version will be redacted. References to protected witnesses in this version will be redacted. There will be two decisions at the beginning of next week; one will be a corrigendum that will refer to paragraph 79 and the corrected Annex A, and there will be a public version of the decision. It will be an almost identical copy of the confidential decision, but references to protected witnesses will be redacted. References to documents that have to do with protected witnesses will be redacted. So these are two future written decisions that will be rendered, decisions which relate to the issue of documents. Ms. Benjamin, is there anything you would like to say with regard to the documents? But the registrar should be provided with the documents so that he can assign them exhibit numbers. The binders of the documents from 1 to 659 in Annex 1 [as interpreted], minus the documents that were withdrawn, naturally, these documents -- this binder must be provided to the registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, the registrar has already been provided with the binders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, the registrar has actually shown me that he has the documents on his right. The registrar could perhaps point to the binders. That will enable the camera to capture the moment. So the binders are to the registrar's right. Mr. Registrar, as far as Annex A is concerned and the numbers for the documents, could you tell us briefly the numbers that will be used.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the documents get the exhibit numbers indicated in your annex to the decision, and into the corrigendum you're going to file, and they are roughly from P403 until P922.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Yes, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Then the -- there will be a summary number, P923, for contested document 10, which is P411; contested document 11, which is P412; contested document 12, which is P413; contested document 13, which is P414; contested document 163, which is P548; contested document 174, which is P557; contested document 445, which is P794, and the relative English translations get the summary number P923/E. There will be a summary number P924 for the following documents: Contested document 20, which is P421; contested document 27, which is P428; contested document 28, which is P429; contested document 229, which is P604; contested document 288, which is P659; contested document 297, which is P667. The relative English translation get the summary number P924/E. There will be a summary number P925 for the following documents: Contested document 231, which is Exhibit P606; contested document 240, which is Exhibit P614; contested document 339, which is Exhibit P705; contested document 345, which is Exhibit P711. The relative English translations get the exhibit number P925/E. There will be a summary number P926 for the following documents: Contested document 173, which is Exhibit P556; contested document 243, which is Exhibit P617; contested document 346, which is P712; contested document 557, which is P884. The relative English translations get the exhibit number P926/E. There will be a summary number P927 for the following documents: Contested document 141, which is P529; contested document 350, which is P716; contested document 452, which is P801. And the relative English translations get the summary number P927/E. And finally, there will be the summary number P928 for the following documents: Contested document 555, which is P882; and contested document 556, which is P883. And the relevant English translations get the summary number P928/E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar, for your assistance with regard to the documents that will be under P923 up until P928. As you have said -- as you have seen, both the Prosecution and the Defence, from Annex A the first exhibit is number 2 to 403, P403, and onwards, so all the documents follow this order, chronological order. And on the last page of Annex A, we arrive at document 658, which will have the number P992. As far as the numbers are concerned, has everything been correctly registered for the Defence? Are there any issues that require clarification? Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The Defence would like to thank the Chamber for its decision on the documents and also for the registrar's work. We have no comments, no submissions we would like to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. I'll now address Mr. Kubura's Defence team. You may take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have no comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. As we have now dealt with the issue of documents, I will now turn to Ms. Benjamin, who may take the floor in order to make submissions with regard to the completion of the presentation of the Prosecution's case. Ms. Benjamin.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, before we go into that aspect, there were some omissions with respect to a few documents. And in agreement with the Defence, we thought it best that the corrections be placed on the record, so I'd just like to go through these, please, now. The bundle referring to the documents have already been passed to the registrar and to the Defence, but we have some for the Judges. And we'll begin with Prosecution Exhibit P145. The correction there is that the original document stated the "year 2, Article 4." It's "year 2, Issue 8," and that has been corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first exhibit is 153.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. For P145, you were saying?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: P145, it was described as "year 2, Article 4"; in fact, it's "year 2, Issue A." That has been corrected. With respect to P153, the full document has now been submitted. With respect to Prosecution Exhibit P180, the date --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. You say that for document -- you say that as far as P153 is concerned - we have it before us - there is a problem. What was the problem?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, the English original was incomplete, and we have now replaced it with the full document. And I'm just told by the registrar that it is going to be replaced officially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. The original tendered version will be replaced by the new P153.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Then we go to Prosecution Exhibit P180. The date mentioned was 20th October 1993, but in fact the date is 30th October 1993. That has been corrected. Prosecution Exhibit P213 -- sorry, Prosecution Exhibit 211. The exact translation has now been provided. Prosecution Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The old version of P211/E is replaced by the new version tendered today.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 213, the revised translation for the version was provided. Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The old version of P213/BCS is replaced by the new version provided today. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 222, the date was corrected. Instead of 26 April 1994, the correct date of 26 February 1994 was provided. Prosecution Exhibit 244, the same position; dated 1 September 1992 has now been provided. The correct date is 11 September 1992. Prosecution 258, the complete original has now been provided.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The old version of P258 is replaced by the new version tendered today.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 308, the correct date was provided; it was wrongly described as dated 26 November 1993. The correct date of 27 July 1993 was provided. Prosecution Exhibit 316, the completed document is now provided.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The old version of P316 is replaced by the new version provided today.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 3308, wrongly described as dated 14th December 1992. The new description, dated 22nd December 1992 has been provided. Prosecution Exhibit 333, wrong date provided, 28 January 1993; the new date, 29 January 1993 has been provided. And Prosecution Exhibit 374/E, the full translation has now been provided.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The old version of P374/E is replaced by the new version tendered today.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, those are the relevant corrections with respect to the documents. But before we get to the end, Mr. President, I would really like to ask if we could go into private session so that I can -- please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session. Ms. Benjamin, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the Prosecution, having presented fully its evidence to the Trial Chamber, wishes first to thank the Trial Chamber for its patience that it has exhibited during the conduct of the Prosecution's case with the Prosecution, and the Prosecution wishes to formally now close the Prosecution's case at this stage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So the Chamber takes note of the fact that the Prosecution has completed the presentation of its case. Before closing this hearing, Mr. Bourgon wanted to take the floor, but the Registrar has something to tell me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I give the floor to the registrar, who has some precisions to make.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may make a correction. In the transcript of the 28th of June, 2004, you can read that the Defence submitted document DH337 and DH337/E. That's not -- that's not right. The Prosecution submitted only a document DH337, which is an English translation of the Yugoslav Criminal Procedure Code -- the Defence. The same with document DH338. In the transcript, you can read that the Defence would have submitted a document DH338 and the document DH338/E. In fact, the Defence submitted only a document DH338, which is an English translation of the Criminal Code of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a point of clarification regarding the transcript of the sitting on the 28th of June, 2004, especially with regard to Exhibit DH338 and DH337. So the Chamber takes note of what you have said. Mr. Bourgon, do you wish to say what you have to say in the presence of everyone? It's up to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should prefer to make this short statement in the absence of the accused, as it does not affect them at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, I should like to ask the security officers to accompany the accused out, and we wish to tell them that we shall meet again at the beginning of October, when the proceedings will be resumed. Could the security officers accompany the accused out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Theoretically the hearing is completed, so your statement is going to be made in the absence of the accused and the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, with the permission of the Chamber, I would like to make this brief statement, certainly in my personal name, as it is -- it has to do with an important situation that affects me personally. Mr. President, on the 23rd of June, I conveyed to the Chamber the following events connected with interviews of witnesses by the Prosecutor, with Defence witnesses in Sarajevo, during which I qualified an administrative decision taken by the Registrar personnel as unreasonable. The next day in my absence, the Registrar, through the registrar of this hearing, called in question my personal integrity, alleging that I had presented the facts to the Chamber in an incomplete and inexact manner. The Registrar added that the Registrar of the Tribunal intended to submit to the Chamber a memorandum, which was indeed done on the 9th of July. Mr. President, I consider that what was said by the Registrar with regard to me was very serious, as it affects my credibility. Also, with regard to the prejudice that may affect the client that I have the honour of representing before this Chamber, and in view of the statement of the Registrar and the memorandum filed on the 9th of July, requires certain commentaries on my part, which I will certainly convey in writing in the near future. Also, in view of my position as President of the Association of Defence Counsel with this International Tribunal, I wish to delay the submission of this written statement, since the Association of Defence Counsel is currently engaged in a process of consultations with the Registrar regarding the norms that affect all Defence counsel, and I would not like my personal problem to overshadow this process, which in my opinion is far more important than my personal situation. Finally, Mr. President, I wish to ask for the indulgence of the Chamber and respectfully to request that it draw no conclusions from these events before I have had a chance to convey my arguments in writing. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. As you tell us, you will file a memorandum following the memorandum of the 9th of July, responding to all that was said in the Registry memo, but you prefer to delay that, as you are negotiating with the Registrar on behalf of all the Defence counsel in this Tribunal certain important matters and this is not of such immediate urgency. And I thank you. We will now adjourn the hearing, and I have been told by the registrar that in the near future he will be replaced by the colleague on his left. I wish to thank him for everything that he has done so far, especially in connection with the numbering of the exhibits in this case, for which the Chamber is especially grateful to him, and by wish him, as we do to everyone in this courtroom, a good rest in the following few weeks. I thank you all. And you will be informed when the proceedings will be resumed in due course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened sine die. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.09 a.m.,
